title: Croque Monsieur
subtitle: French béchamel ham and Gruyère toasted sandwich
excerpt: The Parisian brasserie classic: thick bread spread with béchamel, layered with cooked ham and Gruyère, and either toasted in a pan or baked in the oven until the cheese is bubbling and golden. Simple and very satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: The croque monsieur (crunchy mister) first appeared on Parisian café menus around 1910, though a similar dish of toasted ham and cheese likely predates the name. It is the defining café snack of France: available at every brasserie, served at all hours, and eaten standing at the bar or sitting at a pavement table. The defining element that separates a croque monsieur from a plain toasted sandwich is the béchamel: the sauce is spread both inside the sandwich (with the ham) and on top of the finished sandwich before the final grilling. The croque madame is the same dish with a fried or poached egg on top. Gruyère is the traditional cheese; Emmental also works. The bread should be substantial enough to hold the filling: pain de mie (enriched white bread) or a good white sandwich loaf is ideal.

content.text: The béchamel should be fairly thick so it does not run off the bread. Season it well with salt, pepper, nutmeg, and a little Dijon mustard. The sandwich is best finished under a hot grill: the heat from above browns and bubbles the cheese and sauce on the outside. Watch it closely; it can go from golden to burnt quickly.

items.preparation: thick slices of white sandwich bread or pain de mie

content.text: Make the béchamel: melt the butter in a small pan, add the flour, stir for 1 minute. Gradually add the milk, whisking, and cook for 3 minutes until thick and smooth. Season with salt, pepper, nutmeg, and the mustard. Remove from the heat.

Toast the bread lightly. Spread a thin layer of béchamel on one side of each slice. Lay the ham on 2 slices and top with half the grated Gruyère. Close the sandwiches. Spread the remaining béchamel on top of the sandwiches and scatter with the remaining Gruyère.

Place the sandwiches on a baking sheet under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese on top is bubbling and golden in patches. Watch closely. Alternatively, bake at 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6 for 10 minutes, then briefly under the grill. Serve immediately.
